[ASSISTANT] Tea tree oil is known for its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties that may help to treat acne and other skin conditions.  
[ASSISTANT] The proper application method for tea tree oil includes diluting it with a carrier oil in a 1:10 ratio, cleansing the skin, applying the mixture, and allowing it to dry.  
[ASSISTANT] It is recommended to conduct a patch test before applying diluted tea tree oil to ensure no allergic reactions occur.  
[ASSISTANT] Tea tree oil may help to reduce the appearance of scars and dark spots due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties.  
[ASSISTANT] Tea tree oil should not be applied directly to the skin as it can cause irritation; it must be diluted first.  
[ASSISTANT] For treating dandruff, tea tree oil should be diluted in a 1:10 ratio with a carrier oil before application to the scalp.  
[ASSISTANT] The application method for dandruff includes applying the diluted mixture to the scalp, leaving it on for a few hours or overnight, and washing it out with a mild shampoo.  
[ASSISTANT] Tea tree oil can also be used to treat other scalp conditions such as itchiness and flakiness, following the same dilution and application method as for dandruff.  
[ASSISTANT] Tea tree oil can be used to treat fungal infections on the feet, such as athlete's foot, and should be diluted before application.  
[ASSISTANT] The application method for athlete's foot includes cleansing the feet, applying the diluted mixture, letting it dry, and repeating the process twice a day.  
[ASSISTANT] Tea tree oil can be used as a natural insect repellent, but it should be diluted with a carrier oil before applying to the skin.  
[ASSISTANT] To use tea tree oil as an insect repellent, mix it with a carrier oil and apply it to exposed skin, reapplying as necessary.  
[ASSISTANT] Another method for using tea tree oil as an insect repellent is to mix it with water in a spray bottle and spray it around the house.  
[ASSISTANT] It is emphasized that tea tree oil should never be applied directly to the skin to avoid irritation or allergic reactions.
